headline: GOLD SLIPS to Near Two-Month Low of $4,433; Silver Drops 3% as Dollar Surge, Iran War Fears Weigh
snippet: Gold fell 1.26% to $4,449 while silver dropped 2.94% to $74.58 on May 27, with both metals down roughly 3% on the week. A dollar index above 98.5, 10-year Treasury yields at 4.3–4.4%, and a 58% market probability of a pre-year-end Fed rate hike are maintaining real-yield headwinds against non-yielding bullion — even as Iran ceasefire talks paradoxically eased the safe-haven bid.

headline: GIANTS vs. UNDERDOGS: SSR Mining Emerges as the Cheaper Bet Over Newmont With $1.5B Mine Sale in Play
snippet: Fresh May 27 analysis pits Newmont's $22.7B revenue and nine-country asset base against SSR Mining's net-cash balance sheet and a pending $1.5 billion divestiture of its most troubled mine. SSR trades at a cheaper forward P/E and P/S ratio — and the mine sale creates a near-term catalyst that Newmont's size cannot match.

headline: ATHABASCA STRIKE: Cosa Resources Confirms 1.7% U3O8 in 5-Metre Interval at Murphy Lake North JV with Denison
snippet: Chemical assays released May 26 confirmed hole MLN26-013 hit 0.55% U3O8 over 5.0 metres (308.5–313.5m depth), with a peak of 1.7% U3O8 over 0.5 metres at the Murphy Lake North project — a JV with Denison Mines located 3 km east of IsoEnergy's Hurricane deposit in Saskatchewan's eastern Athabasca Basin. The intersection also returned anomalous nickel and cobalt, hallmarks of the polymetallic system style seen at nearby deposits.

headline: DRILLS TURNING in Colombia: GoldMining Commences Core Program at 100%-Owned Yarumalito Gold-Copper Project
snippet: GoldMining Inc. announced May 26 that it has commenced an exploration-focused core drilling program at its 100%-owned Yarumalito Gold-Copper Project, situated in Colombia's Mid Cauca gold-copper belt — one of the most productive gold corridors in South America. The 2026 program is designed to expand the resource base on a project the company controls outright with no JV dilution.

headline: PENTAGON PLAY: USA Rare Earth Has $354M in Defense Contracts and a Live Magnet Plant — Could It Make You a Fortune?
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) has commissioned Phase 1a of its magnet manufacturing plant and reported $6 million in Q1 2026 sales, with $354 million in Pentagon contracts anchoring its near-term revenue. The company is building the only heavy rare earth processing and magnet manufacturing capability in the Western Hemisphere — but remains pre-profitability in a sector where China still controls 90–95% of global processing.

headline: SIX STRAIGHT DEFICITS: Silver's 762M-Oz Cumulative Shortfall Keeps Growing — Will the Supply Gap Finally Lift Prices?
snippet: The Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 forecasts the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit at 46.3 million ounces, pushing the cumulative shortfall since 2020 to 762 million ounces — the largest sustained deficit run on record. Yet silver is sliding toward $74 as industrial fabrication is forecast to dip 2% to a four-year low, raising the uncomfortable question of whether structural deficits alone can drive a price recovery.

headline: COPPER COUNTDOWN: Goldman Sees 25%+ Section 232 Tariff by Mid-June as Morgan Stanley Forecasts 600,000-Tonne 2026 Deficit
snippet: Goldman Sachs forecasts a 25% US copper import tariff under Section 232 before mid-June, while Morgan Stanley projects a 600,000-tonne refined copper deficit in 2026 — the largest in over two decades. Supply headwinds are stacking: Chile's national output fell 9% year-on-year in March, Freeport's Grasberg restart was pushed from 2027 to 2028, and Ivanhoe's Kamoa-Kakula processing is constrained by sulfuric acid shortages.

headline: LITHIUM DOUBLES in Q1 2026 — Battery Storage Set to Drive 31% of Total Demand as Market Flips Toward Deficit
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate nearly doubled to US$26,278 per tonne in Q1 2026, driven by a 55% year-on-year surge in energy storage demand following a 71% jump in 2025. Guotai Junan projects battery storage will account for 31% of total lithium consumption in 2026 — up from 23% last year — potentially tipping a market that analysts say could swing from surplus to deficit by 22,000–80,000 tonnes depending on how quickly new supply ramps.

headline: GOLD'S KEY WEEK: $4,400 Support Test Looms as Fed Signals and Dollar Strength Set to Decide Direction May 25–31
snippet: Analysts flagged $4,400 as gold's critical technical support level for the week of May 25–31, with the DXY holding above 98.5 and 10-year Treasury yields at 4.3–4.4% compressing the carry advantage of non-yielding bullion. Central banks added a net 244 tonnes of gold in Q1 2026 alone, providing a structural bid beneath the pullback — but a 58% probability of a pre-year-end rate hike is capping the upside.

headline: FORT KNOX AUDIT PUSH: Trump's Review Rekindles Fears Over U.S. Gold Reserve Quality and Liquidity
snippet: Trump's push for an independent Fort Knox audit has resurfaced a decades-old controversy: the bulk of U.S. gold reserves are held as non-standard 916.7 fine bars that do not qualify as "good delivery" for international settlement. No comprehensive independent audit of U.S. gold has been completed since at least the 1970s, leaving the question of how much liquid, standard-grade gold America actually controls unanswered.
